answer: A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The forge multiplier is published, charged in ridge, and summit lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 20 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2286 identities would post 2904 proofs and burn roughly 77 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
